fix_now.what: worker_idle_retire_seconds > 2147483 (~24.8 days) overflows the 32-bit setTimeout delay; Bun clamps to 1 ms (reproduced: setTimeout(fn, 31536000*1000) fired after 6 ms on Bun 1.3.14), so a 'never' value retires every finished worker ~1 ms after idle. Reject seconds*1000 > 2147483647 in both parsers and the post-resolve guard, message naming the key and pointing at 0 as the disable value; one config.test.ts assertion per source.

Number('  ') is 0 and Number('-0') is -0 (-0 < 0 false): whitespace-only or -0 env value silently disables the timer where the positive twin refuses to start. Trim for the unset check; reject a trimmed value not matching /^\d+$/; assert both throw naming LEGION_WORKER_IDLE_RETIRE_SECONDS.

No committed test fires a superseded clock, so the entry-identity check at processes.ts:1521 (the only guard against a zero-window retirement under real timers, since cancel() resolves the superseded sleep) has no regression lock; the docstring claims otherwise. Add: idle -> running -> idle (two 600_000 waits), fire older -> no shutdown, one wait pending; fire newer -> one shutdown; plus dispose()-then-fire. (code-quality graded this Major; re-graded Minor because shipped behaviour is correct.)

'wakes arrive by a publish that is rejected with no live holder, never by the dead-worker recovery path' is inaccurate for daemon-routed wakes (onUndeliverable index.ts:324-334 and handleException processes.ts:1916-1929 send a sub-architect 404 to resumeWorker). Accurate reason: the root architect reaches its sub-architect by an OMP-side envoy_publish whose 404 returns to the caller and is never routed through the daemon. Reword all three sites.
Tester-rig timings (8.7 min / 5.7 min) in a source comment; drop the parenthetical, 'Scenario:' in the test.

Bullet omits the re-arm-on-decline behaviour added in the corrective round; add the clause (decline on active-phase/pendingAssignment re-arms inside the same critical section -> retired within one further window once the phase moves or the queued task drains; every other decline leaves it unarmed).
